summary: Correction attempt for the independent review. IR-15.2-01: LibraryWorkWorker now keeps the bounded item-id fallback as the subject and retains the existing bounded connection scope and image surface as '<subject> (<connection|*>, <surface>)' in both the processed and retry-scheduled records, so ADR-026 clause 1 replaces only the emitted item identifier; DescribeWorkItem centralizes the format and the tests pin both context components. IR-15.2-02/TQ-15.2-01: the reader-threw metadata-read-failure catch is now a distinct, tested site (path-bearing and pathless theories driving FakeMetadataReader.Handler to throw). IR-15.2-03/TQ-15.2-02: the scheduled-retry record is now driven with a connection-scoped retryable queue item and asserted. IR-15.2-04 is recorded in known_limitations as deferred to task 15.4. The changelog entry and this report were updated so every claim matches the tests: 13 theories / 78 new cases, LogRedactionTests 143 passed, full suite Failed 0 / Passed 1595 / Skipped 63 / Total 1658, build 0 warnings / 0 errors, check-docs PASS.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The artwork coordinator emits the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LogOutcome builds LogSubject.Create(request.JellyfinItemId, request.MediaIdentity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath) and interpolates the subject (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.cs); LogRedactionTests.ArtworkSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts the message contains 'item example.mkv', no '/', and no item identifier at the levels where the Information line is enabled.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The metadata reconciliation processor's metadata-read-failure line emits the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Both MetadataReadFailed paths build the subject from the identity created by MediaIdentityFactory.TryCreate: the reader-threw catch (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs catch block) and the failed-read result. LogRedactionTests.MetadataReadFailureSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity covers the failed-read path, MetadataReaderThrowSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity covers the reader-threw catch (both assert 'item example.mkv', no '/', no item identifier, and pin the path via the failure text), and MetadataReadFailureSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoPathIsAvailable / MetadataReaderThrowSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoPathIsAvailable prove both fall back when the identity has no primary path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Sonarr/Radarr metadata readers emit the file name when the identity/path is available.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: RadarrMetadataReader.LogMatch and SonarrMetadataReader.LogMatch build LogSubject.Create(identity.JellyfinItemId, identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath); LogRedactionTests.RadarrMatchSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'item example.mkv' and SonarrMatchSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'item s02e05.mkv', each with no '/', no item identifier, and no sentinel.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The mixed MetadataReconciliationProcessor.Discard site uses the file name when available and falls back to the item id otherwise; it does not thread a path where none exists.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Discard(Guid, string?, string) builds LogSubject.Create(itemId, primaryPath); the six changed-basis discards after identity creation pass identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath, and the two-argument overload used by the version-mismatch, item-missing, identity-creation-failure, ineligibility, and connection-unavailable discards delegates with null. LogRedactionTests covers the path case, the identity-without-path case, and the no-identity case; each pins the exact discard branch reason.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The work worker and lifecycle removal event use the documented item-id fallback.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LibraryWorkWorker uses LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId) as the subject and retains the bounded connection scope and image surface as '<subject> (<connection|*>, <surface>)' in LogProcessed and LogRetryScheduled; ArrTagsLifecycleService builds LogSubject.Create(e.ItemId) for the item-removed record. LogRedactionTests.WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity (processed, hint-derived key), WorkWorkerRetrySubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity (scheduled retry, connection-scoped key), and LifecycleRemovalSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity assert the D-format item identifier, no '/', no file name, and no sentinel at every verbosity; the worker theories also pin the retained '<connection|*>, <surface>' context (ADR-026 clause 1 replaces only the item identifier).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Per-site tests prove no directory appears and that the mixed site falls back correctly.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AssertFileNameSubject asserts the message names 'item <file name>', contains no '/', and no longer contains the replaced item identifier; AssertItemIdSubject asserts 'item <D-format id>', no '/', and neither file name. The 13 theories run over all six verbosity levels; AssertNoSentinel(run) is asserted on every case, including the levels where the line is gated off (record count 0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Phase 15 threading portion: the file-name-only subject is emitted where a path is available and the item id where it is not, including the mixed discard site.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The code changes and the 78 new LogRedactionTests cases above; the remaining phase-15 criteria (bounded render classification, ADR-020 clause 4 amendment, canonical documentation, security review, F8 resolution) are owned by tasks 15.3 and 15.4 and are untouched.

interpretations.question: Which available identity's path the mixed discard threads when both the basis identity and the publish-time re-resolved identity exist.
interpretations.chosen: The basis identity created at the metadata-read stage (identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath) at all six post-identity discards.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 3 describes the mixed site as called 'where an identity exists (changed-basis discards after identity creation)'; the basis identity is the identity the queued work was based on and the only one present at every such branch (the publish-time TryCreate can fail).
interpretations.impact: At a changed-basis discard the log names the file observed when the work's identity was captured; if the item's primary path changes within that processing window, the earlier file name is emitted. Log output only; no persisted state or user-visible behavior.

interpretations.question: Which code paths constitute 'the metadata-read-failure line' in the processor.
interpretations.chosen: Both provider-error paths that emit ArrTagsLogEvent.MetadataReadFailed: the reader-threw catch and the failed-read result, each now covered by its own path-bearing and pathless theories.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 3 names the identity-bearing metadata-read-failure line by its event/shape; both paths emit the identical message shape after identity creation and before the same fallback semantics apply.
interpretations.impact: Consistent subjects on both failure paths; no behavior change beyond the subject.

interpretations.question: How the worker's bounded connection scope and image surface are retained once the subject is the item-identifier fallback (IR-15.2-01).
interpretations.chosen: Emit '<subject> (<connection|*>, <surface>)': the item-id fallback subject followed by the same bounded connection scope and surface values the pre-task WorkItemKey text carried, centralized in DescribeWorkItem.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 1 replaces the emitted Jellyfin item identifier only, and ADR-020 clause 4 already permits the connection identity; WorkItemKey documents its connection id and surface as bounded, non-secret diagnostics. Dropping them would be diagnostic loss beyond the task's scope.
interpretations.impact: The worker records keep the connection/surface context; the item-id component changes from N format to the D-format subject and the 'WorkItemKey(...)' wrapper becomes parentheses. No persisted state or non-log behavior changes.

test_sensitivity: Probe round A (22 failures / 143): reverting the artwork subject to the raw item id failed 3 cases (Information, Debug, Trace); reverting the failed-read and reader-threw subjects to LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId) failed 4 cases each (Warning and above); reverting the Radarr and Sonarr LogMatch subjects failed 2 cases each (Debug, Trace); ignoring primaryPath in the three-argument Discard helper failed the mixed path theory 3 cases (Information and above); reverting the worker context to the pre-task WorkItemKey text failed the processed and scheduled-retry theories 2 cases each (Debug, Trace). Probes reverted.

Probe round B (20 failures / 143): replacing the failed-read and reader-threw fallbacks with a non-item-id subject failed 4 cases each; breaking the discard fallback failed the identity-without-path and no-identity theories 3 cases each; emitting an N-format identifier at the lifecycle-removal site failed its theory 2 cases (Debug, Trace); dropping the retained worker connection/surface context failed the processed and retry context assertions 2 cases each. Probes reverted.

The reader-threw coverage added for IR-15.2-02/TQ-15.2-01 fails when either the catch-path subject substitution is reverted (round A: 4 file-name cases) or its fallback is broken (round B: 4 fallback cases), proving the new site is exercised and asserted.

The scheduled-retry coverage added for IR-15.2-03/TQ-15.2-02 fails when the retry record's subject is reverted (round A: 2 cases) and when the retained connection/surface context is dropped (round B: 2 cases), proving the WorkItemRetryScheduled record is exercised and asserted.

The lifecycle site's item-id fallback is byte-identical to its pre-task D-format output, so reverting that site to its pre-task code cannot fail the test by construction; the probe used a different subject format (N) to show the assertion is sensitive.
All probes were applied as direct source edits and reverted by restoring byte-identical copies (diff clean); the final LogRedactionTests run passed 143/143 and the final full suite passed 1595/1658.

known_limitations: The explicit fallback boundaries (LibraryWorkWorker, ArrTagsLifecycleService) and the pre-identity metadata discards emit the item identifier and never a file name; this is the ADR-026 clause 3 documented behavior for boundaries with no media identity or path. The worker records retain the bounded connection scope and surface alongside the subject; the lifecycle-removal output is byte-identical to its pre-task D-format item id.

At a changed-basis discard the emitted name is the file name from the identity captured at the metadata-read stage, not a re-read path: if the item's primary path changes within the same processing window after identity creation, the discard line carries the earlier file name. Log output only; no persisted state or user-visible behavior.

IR-15.2-04: ADR-026 clause 3's parenthetical is inaccurate for the ineligible and connection-unavailable pre-publish discards (they run after identity creation, where a path is available) and does not name the missing-kind discard. The implementation follows the clause 3 enumeration and threads no path at those sites; reconciling the ADR wording with the actual call sites is deferred to task 15.4 (no change required for 15.2).

F8 remains open. Task 15.3 owns emitting the bounded render classification on the artwork log line, and task 15.4 owns the ADR-020 clause 4 amendment, the README/architecture/limitations reconciliation, the logging security review, and the F8 resolution; until 15.4 those current-state documents continue to describe the shipped v1.1 logging behavior.
